patterns_data.pattern_details: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend increased sharply, led first by a large jump in admissions and then reinforced by higher paid per admit in key medical DRGs. The increase is concentrated in urinary infection, kidney, metabolic and electrolyte, and cardiac admissions rather than a broad-based inpatient rise. This is a combined utilization and unit-cost problem in a focused inpatient case mix.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the largest actionable cost pattern and points to specific admission management and reimbursement levers in TX DSNP inpatient care.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a TX DSNP inpatient action plan focused on kidney/UTI, metabolic-electrolyte, and cardiac DRGs, combining UM review of avoidable admissions with reimbursement review of the highest-cost acute hospital facilities.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital utilization added $48.3M, with 2,169 more admissions and 2,536 more claims.
A further $2.3M of TX DSNP acute hospital pressure came from both volume and higher paid per admit, including about +$2.7K in metabolic/electrolyte DRGs and +$9.2K in kidney/UTI with MCC.
TX clinical case mix added $3.2M, led by UTI SITE NOT SPECIFIED at $1.1M on 96 admissions and ACUTE CYSTITIS WITHOUT HEMATURIA at $0.5M.

patterns_data.pattern_details: This pattern is driven by one-off or very low-frequency catastrophic inpatient cases rather than a recurring utilization trend. Several of the largest cases sit at UHCMC and THE CLEVELAND CLINIC FOUNDATION, with very high paid per admit on complex airway, hematology, and surgical admissions. These cases need claim-level confirmation and clinical review before any broader policy response.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Rare catastrophic cases can be financially material, but they require case-level handling so the organization does not mistake them for a scalable trend.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Open a case-level audit for each high-dollar outlier to confirm eligibility, payment accuracy, provider contract application, and whether any should be carved out from broader trend actions.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is dominated by low-volume, often single-admission outliers and includes unattributed cases, so case-level validation is required.
evidence_summary: Rare high-cost cases across CA, OH, TX, and UNATTRIBUTED added $1.4M overall.
The largest single case was UHCMC at $401K for tracheostomy with prolonged mechanical ventilation tied to ACQUIRED HEMOPHILIA.
THE CLEVELAND CLINIC FOUNDATION added a separate $261K connective tissue disorder case, and KAWEAH DELTA HEALTH CARE added a $74K coronary bypass case.
